newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Nov key M2 money +9.7 pct yr/yr (+9.8 pct).
newsitem.headline: Czech Nov key M2 money +9.7 pct yr/yr (+9.8 pct).

text.p: The Czech Republic's key money supply measure, M2, was 9.7 percent higher at the end of November, year-on-year, after 9.8 percent year-on-year growth to the end of October, the central bank said on Thursday.
The central bank added in a statement that excluding the funds from the sale of an equity stake in telephone operator SPT Telecom, M2 grew by 11.3 percent, year-on-year, to the end of November.
CZECH M2 MONEY NOV 1996 OCT 1996 NOV 1995
Note. All 1996 figures subject to revision. Czech M2 measures currency, demand deposits, time and savings deposits, and foreign currency deposits.
The bottom figures exlude the effect of SPT Telecom's $1.32 billion equity expansion in the summer of 1995 which was put on deposit at the Czech National Bank (CNB).
The CNB statement said that total crown and foreign currency credits obtained by bank clients grew by 10.5 percent, year-on-year, following 10.7 percent year-on-year growth in October.
It added that total crown and foreign currency deposits at banks, including funds from SPT Telecom, grew by 8.8 percent, year-on-year, following 8.6 percent year-on-year growth in October.
The statement said the average interest rate on new crown credits drawn at banks in November was 13.86 percent, some eight basis points higher than October.
